caption:
And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed, 'If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe.'

Surah Ibrahim (14:7). Swipe through for the Arabic, then English, Mandarin, Korean, Japanese and Malay.

Sources on the final slide.

#Quran #Ibrahim #Shukr #IslamicReminder #Deen

sourcing.primary_text: Qur'an 14:7, Surah Ibrahim, in which Allah proclaims that gratitude (shukr) brings increase while ingratitude brings severe punishment - a short, complete, mainstream single-ayah statement on gratitude, chosen as today's second post after reviewing candidates outside the surahs already covered by the 29 published posts (first Surah Ibrahim post). No restricted-addressee or sensitive-scope nuance, and its theme (gratitude and divine increase) is not yet covered by any published post.
sourcing.arabic: Edition quran-uthmani, api.alquran.cloud/v1/ayah/14:7/editions/quran-uthmani,en.sahih,zh.jian,ko.korean,ja.japanese,ms.basmeih, live-fetched 2026-09-26, HTTP 200. Slide text extracted programmatically from the raw API response field and asserted byte-identical before writing the slide file (an earlier hand-transcribed draft of this slide was caught with three inadvertent character substitutions during this same verification pass and was corrected by re-extracting the field programmatically rather than by hand).
sourcing.english: Edition en.sahih (Saheeh International), same live API call, HTTP 200. The raw source string ends with a stray, unpaired punctuation artifact - a space followed by an orphan straight double-quote with no matching opening double-quote anywhere in the string (the quotation is already fully closed by the paired single quotes around 'If you are grateful ... severe.'). Removed as a punctuation-only formatting artifact; no wording was touched. Extracted programmatically and asserted identical to the source except for this one documented removal.
sourcing.chinese: Edition zh.jian (Ma Jian translation), same live API call, HTTP 200. Extracted programmatically and asserted byte-identical to source. No formatting artifacts.
sourcing.korean: Edition ko.korean, same live API call, HTTP 200. Edition metadata lists englishName 'Unknown' for the translator, so the citation slide reads 'translator not specified by source'. The raw source string had four stray inserted spaces splitting single words, the same recurring artifact type seen on this edition on prior posts: '것 을' to '것을' (that-which, object marker), '감사 한다면' to '감사한다면' (if grateful), '것이 며' to '것이며' (and-it-is), and '실 로' to '실로' (indeed/truly). No character was added, removed or changed; only whitespace was corrected, applied to the rendered slide only, not the quoted raw source in this note.
sourcing.japanese: Edition ja.japanese, same live API call, HTTP 200. Same 'Unknown' translator metadata as Korean, so the citation slide also reads 'translator not specified by source' for Japanese. Extracted programmatically and asserted byte-identical to source.
sourcing.malay: Edition ms.basmeih (Abdullah Muhammad Basmeih), same live API call, HTTP 200. Extracted programmatically and asserted byte-identical to source. No formatting artifacts.
sourcing.verification_note: All six editions live-fetched in a single API call this session (2026-09-26) from api.alquran.cloud, HTTP 200. Every slide's text asserted byte-for-byte equal to the corresponding API response field programmatically in code before publishing was attempted (Korean diverges only by the four documented whitespace fixes; English diverges only by the one documented trailing-artifact removal). Caption pull-quote asserted equal to the corrected English text. No wording generated from memory.
sourcing.compliance_check: Checked programmatically this session against every string term in scripts/data/compliance-policy.json's halal section (prohibited, superstition, origins_patterns; 123 terms) across all slide text, title, caption and tags, using word-boundary regex matching. No hits. Pure typography, no imagery, so animate_imagery and context_review do not apply. House style: no em or en dashes, no emoji, UK spelling used throughout the caption.
